detail.text: What is left is exactly the integral points of one elliptic curve, 37.a1: the LMFDB computes them from a Mordell–Weil basis with an elliptic-logarithm bound (Stroeker–Tzanakis 1994; Sage/Magma IntegralPoints). Mathlib has neither Mordell–Weil for a specific curve nor a Baker-type lower bound for linear forms in elliptic logarithms, so the hole is not formalisable today and is not split further: any split would be a restatement. route.text: Reduce the pair equation to integral points on the minimal model of the elliptic curve 37.a1 (y^2 + y = x^3 - x) by x = n - 1, y = m(m-3)/2; partial PR #1171 proves the map and reads the binomial solutions off the curve's integral points, one hole = that list.
